An intermediate uniform-pixel interpolation shortcut was rejected and removed after paired nineteen-image cost was slower on both cache domains. Its passing tests and observed losses remain in the retained rejected-candidate archive, not the qualified product results.
AttributionLimits: This follow-up records 219/267 correct positive images versus 219/267 previously; gained: none; previously correct positive images lost: none. Paired negative completion is [28, 22, 30, 30]/31 currently and [28, 29, 30, 30]/31 previously. The seeded QR fine search changes no recognition hypothesis. Paired nineteen-image costs and nine-request retail costs remain separate, with every sample and recognition failure retained. No recognition allowance, hint, oracle or scoring change. Supplemental PDF417 images are regression evidence informed by prior remediation, not an unseen holdout. Invalid GS1 AI (3922) oracles and undeclared QR encoding policies remain unchanged. Shared-host contention and budgets affect results. Stacked DataBar/Expanded Stacked multiple-symbol localization and arbitrary perspective remain unproved; MaxiCode image scanning is unsupported. These finite workloads do not establish overall superiority.

QrSamplingProof.Limits: Task-local reflection proof over independent grayscale, binary, patterned and gradient fields, each with and without local thresholds, inversion, fractional geometry and QR dimensions 21 through 177. Exact output-double bits and direct sample bytes compared, including all 256 uniform byte values, clamped borders, nonuniform blocks and one-pixel differences. Cost is refinement only, not a decoder ranking. No production hooks added. Supersedes earlier preliminary synthetic proofs with incorrect switch-expression precedence and coupled pattern/map selection.

PairedDecodeCost.Scope: Same nineteen preloaded RGBA32 images, options and 1500 ms allowance as the decoding comparison.
